basis: First review after edit (pass_seq 1). Read as the exam coach: signals and their 'but not if' guards in 1-fast.md and 2-deep.md, traps, comparison tables, the 18 shipped questions of 5-quiz.md and their JSON in data/14-elb/questions.json (9 core, 9 extended; 2 multi; twin pairs q002/q006 and q013/q017), cards and speak items, against the registry bullets of chapter 14 and _build/spec/FREQUENCY.md (research input, not evidence). Every registry bullet (1.3.S3, 2.1.K9, 2.1.K10, 2.2.K8, 2.2.S4, 3.4.K3, 3.4.S4, 4.2.S1, 4.4.K3) has a section and at least one shipped question.

findings.quote: Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
findings.evidence: 14 of the 18 shipped questions use 'LEAST operational overhead' (elb-q003, q004, q008, q010, q011, q013, q014, q015, q016, q017, q018, q019, q020, q022); 3 use MOST cost-effective (q001, q002, q006) and 1 MOST secure (q005). No shipped question asks for HIGHEST availability, LOWEST latency or MOST performant, although SPEC.json questions.qualifier_words lists HIGHEST, LOWEST and FASTEST, and task 3.4 (high-performing networks) is one of the chapter's tasks. With this mix the reader learns that every ELB question is an operations question and stops reading the qualifier, which is the habit READER.md says to train out ('Train her to find the constraint in the stem'). Rewrite two or three extended items (for example q016 and q008) with a performance or availability qualifier.
findings.resolution: fix-14: partly addressed, rest deferred. The shipped set now swaps elb-q018 (LEAST operational overhead) for the verified elb-q021 (MOST secure), so the mix is 13 / 3 / 2. Rewriting the qualifier of q016 or q008 changes their stems and can change which option is best, so each would need a new verification round (R5 reset); the items are correct as verified. Reported for the next question round: two extended items with HIGHEST availability or LOWEST latency.

findings.evidence: Shipped difficulty counts: 1 = 3 (q001, q003, q015), 2 = 12, 3 = 3 (q008, q016, q019). Share of difficulty 2 is 12/18 = 0.67, above SPEC.json questions.difficulty_mix '2': 0.55 plus difficulty_mix_tolerance 0.1 = 0.65; difficulty 3 is 0.17 against a target of 0.25. Move one difficulty-2 item to 3 (q005 with a TLS-listener distractor that keeps path routing is a candidate) or ship one of the verified level-3 items (q012, q021) in place of a level-2 one.
findings.resolution: fix-14: the verified level-3 item elb-q021 (edited-pass, 3.4.K3, extended) is now shipped and the level-2 extended item elb-q018 went back to verified (set-status). Shipped difficulty: 1 = 3, 2 = 11, 3 = 4 (0.61 for level 2, inside the tolerance). 2.2.K8 stays covered by elb-q011; q lint 14 --ship clean (18 ready, 9 core, 9 extended, 2 multi, 2 twin pairs).

findings.quote: | "route by URL path or host name" | ALB listener rules | rules [forward requests based on the URL](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-path-conditions-smaller-services) | fixed addresses too: an NLB in front |
findings.evidence: A 'but not if' guard must name the case where the 'Think' answer is wrong. Here the ALB stays the answer: with fixed addresses too, the design is an NLB in front of the ALB, which keeps the ALB rules (fact elb-nlb-alb-target-combines-features, 'takes over the load balancing decision'; elb-q008 key). A reader who skims the row reads 'fixed addresses: NLB' and picks the NLB-replaces-ALB distractor that elb-q008 and elb-q002 are built around. Write 'fixed addresses too: keep the ALB behind an NLB', or replace the guard with a real exception (TCP or UDP traffic with no HTTP: an NLB).
findings.resolution: fix-14: the guard now reads 'fixed addresses too: keep the ALB, add an NLB in front'.

findings.quote: With Elastic IP addresses, its addresses [must be completely controlled by you](../facts/elb.md#elb-nlb-faq-no-mix-eip-and-elb-ips), so the [addresses known to your clients do not change](../facts/elb.md#elb-nlb-faq-no-mix-eip-and-elb-ips).
findings.evidence: Fact elb-nlb-faq-no-mix-eip-and-elb-ips is the rule against mixing ELB-provided and Elastic IP addresses on one NLB (claim: 'cannot mix ELB-provided IPs with Elastic IPs'); it is not why an NLB has fixed addresses. The explanation should teach the deciding mechanism: one static address per zone, with an optional Elastic IP address per subnet (fact elb-nlb-static-ip-per-az-optional-eip, already linked in the twin line), against ALB node addresses that 'can be remapped quickly' (elb-dns-ttl-60-seconds-remap). Same wrong cause as reader-03 in 2-deep.md.
findings.resolution: fix-14: explanation only (stem, options and key unchanged, so the passed verification stands): 'In each zone, Elastic Load Balancing creates a network interface and [uses it to get a static IP address](elb-nlb-static-ip-per-az-optional-eip), while an ALB's node [IP addresses can be remapped quickly](elb-dns-ttl-60-seconds-remap).' Both facts were already in the item's facts; q lint clean.

findings.quote: Cross-zone load balancing is turned off for the target group, and zonal shift is turned on for the load balancer.
findings.evidence: The stem names the feature that the key uses ('Start a zonal shift ...'), so a reader can match words instead of reasoning; the deciding phrase should be 'still pass their health checks'. Real exam stems describe the situation, not the setting that the answer needs. Keep the precondition out of the stem (the key can say 'turn on zonal shift and start a zonal shift', grounded in elb-alb-zonal-shift-off-by-default-one-az) or move it into every option. Also: the key names Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), which 2-deep.md never names (the zonal shift Go deeper block says only 'zonal shift'), so the question tests a name the chapter does not teach.
findings.resolution: fix-14: the teaching gap is fixed: the zonal shift Go deeper of 2-deep.md now names it 'a capability of [Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)](elb-zonal-shift-what)'. The stem cue is deferred: changing the stem and the key text of a verified item can change what the solvers pick, so it needs a new verification round (R5 reset). Reported for the next question round.

findings.quote: Add 2 instances in each Availability Zone, because cross-zone load balancing is already turned on for every type of load balancer.
findings.evidence: The option carries its own false premise in a 'because' clause, so it is eliminated by reading, not by knowing the NLB default; and adding 2 instances to each zone does not change the 2:6 imbalance even if the premise were true, so it fails twice. A plausible distractor states only the action that a person with the misconception would choose and leaves the reader to find the flaw. Replace it with an action whose flaw is the NLB's cross-zone default or its flow hash, for example 'Turn on sticky sessions for the target group so that new clients are spread over all instances' (named misconception: stickiness balances load).
findings.resolution: fix-14: deferred. Replacing an option changes the option set of a verified item, so it needs a new verification round (R5 reset); q016 is correct as verified and is the chapter's only shipped question on the NLB cross-zone default. Reported for the next question revision with the suggested sticky-sessions distractor.

findings.quote: 5. Between the certificate list and three load balancers, the difference is how many resources the team runs and pays for; the stem says LEAST operational overhead, and each load balancer is billed by the hour, so one listener with a certificate list wins.
findings.evidence: This is a worked example, so its think-aloud is the model she copies. It decides a LEAST operational overhead question with an hourly price, and the Why not for the three-ALB option again leads with 'three charges for each hour or partial hour'. Exam items keep cost and operational overhead apart; the deciding reason here is one listener and one set of rules to manage instead of three load balancers. Rewrite step 5 and that Why not line around the work to run and change, and keep the billing fact for the cost question elb-q001.
findings.resolution: fix-14: worked step 5 now reads '... the difference is how much the team must run and change; the stem says LEAST operational overhead, so one listener with one set of rules wins over three load balancers with three listeners.' Option b why now reads 'Three load balancers mean three listeners and three sets of rules to run and change, where one listener with a certificate list is enough.' Explanation fields only; stem, options and key unchanged; q lint clean.

findings.section: Listener rules are checked in priority order and the default rule comes last
findings.quote: 4. **Act.** The rule forwards, returns a fixed response, or redirects, for example from [HTTP to HTTPS](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-redirect-http-to-https).
findings.evidence: User authentication at the ALB (authenticate with an OIDC identity provider or an Amazon Cognito user pool before forwarding) is a common security pattern for task 1.x and is missing from the action list and from the questions. The canon has the fact (elb-alb-user-authentication-idps, verified), and card elb-c032 already asks 'which load balancer can sign users in before requests reach the application?' with nothing in the chapter that teaches it. Add 'authenticates users' to step 4 with that fact link, and a signal row ('sign users in at the load balancer, no code change' -> ALB authenticate action; but not if: the API needs per-client throttling -> API Gateway).
findings.resolution: fix-14: step 4 now teaches it (same fix as claims-07): an HTTPS listener rule can add [a user authentication action and a routing action], with sign-in through an [OpenID Connect (OIDC) compliant] provider or Amazon Cognito. The signal row was not added: the fast signals table is at its maximum of 8 rows (SPEC signal_rows) and the section is already over its word budget. No new question (a new item needs its own verification); reported for the next question round.

findings.quote: | "replace unhealthy instances automatically" | Auto Scaling group with ELB health checks |
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md row 'ELB vs Route 53 vs EC2 health checks' reports this pair as commonly asked ('ASG should use the ELB health check type for app-level health; DNS failover -> Route 53'). The chapter covers EC2 status checks vs ELB checks (elb-q011) but never contrasts the load balancer's health checks with Route 53 health checks and DNS failover between load balancers or Regions; the only multi-Region answer it gives is Global Accelerator. Add one signals row or trap with an xref to the Route 53 chapter ('fail over to another Region' -> Route 53 failover records with health checks; the load balancer only routes inside its Region), grounded in facts from that chapter's canon.
findings.resolution: fix-14: deferred. The fast signals table is at its maximum of 8 rows and the trap list at its maximum of 5 (SPEC counts), and the Route 53 failover facts belong to the Route 53 chapter's canon. Reported to the orchestrator for the Route 53 chapter's signals (load balancer health checks route inside one Region; Route 53 failover records move traffic between Regions).

findings.quote:
**FAQ 7.** Can an NLB accept TCP and UDP on one port?
...
> "You must associate a TCP+UDP listener with a TCP+UDP target group."
findings.evidence: The quoted sentence does not answer the question: it says nothing about one port. The same fact (elb-nlb-faq-tcp-udp-same-port, source www/elasticloadbalancing/faqs) has the sentence that does: 'For example, for a DNS service using both TCP and UDP, you can create a TCP+UDP listener on port 53, and the load balancer will process traffic for both UDP and TCP requests on that port.' Quote that sentence.
findings.resolution: fix-14: FAQ 7 now quotes that sentence (same fix as claims-16); L306 clean.

findings.section: Cross-zone load balancing spreads requests over the targets in every enabled zone
findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** An ALB target group has cross-zone turned off. Can it hold a Lambda function?
findings.evidence: Three Stop-and-answer items test edge cases instead of the subsection's mechanism: Lambda targets with cross-zone off (here), weighted random with sticky sessions (sticky subsection, fact elb-alb-weighted-random-no-sticky-slow-start), and GWLB 2-tuple stickiness for FTP (GWLB subsection). None of these is in FREQUENCY.md's reported sub-topics, and a Stop-and-answer is the one check per subsection. Move them into the Go deeper blocks and ask the core question instead (for example: 'Cross-zone off, two targets in AZ 1 and six in AZ 2: what share of requests does each AZ 1 target get?'; 'An instance with sticky users is removed at scale-in: what happens to their sessions?').
findings.resolution: fix-14: the core cross-zone case (two targets in AZ 1, six in AZ 2, NLB defaults) is now Check 1 of 1-fast.md, which the reader meets first, and it stays the subject of the shipped elb-q016. The sticky scale-in case is the Exam trap directly above the sticky Stop-and-answer, so asking it again would repeat the trap. 2-deep.md is at its file word ceiling (L201 4,500), so the edge-case items stay as the subsection checks; the GWLB answer now names the default 5-tuple (reader-13).

findings.quote: "extremely low latency, huge request rates" | NLB
findings.evidence: The performance signal of 1-fast ('extremely low latency, huge request rates' -> NLB, but not if AWS WAF rules are needed -> ALB) and the 2-deep signal 'static IP addresses or extreme performance' have no shipped question. The three 3.4 questions (q008, q013, q016, q017) test static IPs, sessions and cross-zone. One extended item on an NLB for a high-rate TCP or UDP workload, with an ALB-plus-WAF twin, would test the guard. The client-IP signal (ALB X-Forwarded-For vs NLB client IP preservation, card elb-c021) also has no question.
findings.resolution: fix-14: deferred. A new question needs the full blind verification (three solvers), which is not part of the fix stage. Reported for the next question round: an NLB high-rate TCP or UDP item with an ALB-plus-WAF twin, and a client-IP item (X-Forwarded-For vs client IP preservation).

findings.quote: | "several HTTPS domains on one load balancer" | certificate list with Server Name Indication (SNI) | ... | one parent domain: a wildcard certificate |
findings.evidence: The guard is unlinked and loose: 'one parent domain' also covers the apex (example.com), which a wildcard *.example.com does not name. Fact elb-alb-cert-wildcard-or-san-single-cert gives the grounded wording: 'you can use a wildcard certificate or add a Subject Alternative Name (SAN) for each additional domain'. Write 'subdomains of one domain: one wildcard or SAN certificate' and link the fact.
findings.resolution: fix-14: the guard now reads 'subdomains of one domain: [use a wildcard certificate](elb-alb-cert-wildcard-or-san-single-cert) or SAN'.
